title: Day 60 · Week 8, Day 4 — Adventure: the long-haul — one clot in four and a half thousand flights, the stocking that stops nine in ten, the eleven percent on the Zika map, mefloquine or elsewhere, and the clause nobody reads
summary: The fifth Adventure episode: Day 32 cleared the short flight; today is the twelve-hour one and the far-away country. Your baby is at the turn of Carnegie stage 18 to 19 (16–18 mm), trunk straightening, hands and feet reaching toward the midline — and reached by an airplane only through your partner's body. Permission: ACOG CO 746 (occasional air travel safe in an uncomplicated pregnancy; seat belt on; cosmic radiation negligible), airlines to 36 weeks and cruise lines to 24 (CDC Yellow Book), some airlines wanting a letter from 28 weeks and some insurers stopping at 32 (EBCOG 2022); 628,292 Israeli births with +9 g and +0.36 days for the 6.6% who flew (Shalev Ram 2020); flight attendants' OR 1.3 (0.9–1.8) (Aspholm 1999); ten wired women with normal fetal heart rates in the air (Huch 1986). The cabin: 1,800–2,500 m equivalent, below the Day 46 sleeping line; SpO2 90–95%; the Hb <8, sickle-cell and cardiopulmonary exceptions; humidity under 10%; a 10-hour flight ≈ 0.05 mGy, half a chest X-ray against the Day 57 50-mGy line. The clot: baseline VTE 0.5–2 per 1,000 pregnancies, 4–5× the non-pregnant rate, 9.3% of US maternal deaths (ACOG PB 196); Kuipers 2007 (8,755 employees, 38,910 person-years, 53 clots): IRR 3.2 after flights ≥4 h, one event per 4,656 long-haul flights, ~1 in 1,264 over 16 h, +10% per hour, +40% per extra flight; MEGA (Cannegieter 2006): pregnancy plus flight OR 14.3, window seat vs aisle OR 2.2; combined, roughly 1 in 1,000 per flight with wide uncertainty — and Cochrane 2021 (12 trials, 2,918 passengers): symptomless DVT 3 vs 47, OR 0.10, high certainty; RCOG stockings for every pregnant woman over 4 h; BSH 2023's 4-hour definition and pregnancy as a risk factor; LMWH only with extra risk factors. Time zones: melatonin works for adults crossing ≥5 zones (Cochrane 2002, NNT ~2) but the NHS says not in pregnancy, so fly west, use daylight, empty the first day. The map: CDC's rule against travel to an active Zika notice; Honein 2017 (442 pregnancies: 6% birth defects, 11% first trimester, same whether symptomatic; baseline microcephaly 7 per 10,000); Brasil 2016 (42% of 117 live infants abnormal; 55% adverse after first-trimester infection); condoms for the whole pregnancy after a partner's exposure. Malaria: worse in pregnancy (Yellow Book); 125.2 million pregnancies a year in transmission areas (Dellicour 2010); 12.4 million African women exposed and 900,000 low-birth-weight babies a year, 65% of placental infections first taking hold at the end of the first trimester (Walker 2014); chloroquine or mefloquine only — doxycycline, primaquine and tafenoquine contraindicated, atovaquone-proguanil not recommended; the net and DEET. Live vaccines off, yellow fever a precaution with a waiver; hepatitis E case fatality 15–25% in pregnancy, so bottled or boiled water and no iodine tablets; azithromycin yes, bismuth no. Arrival altitude by the Day 46 rule. And the clause: CDC's advice to buy cover for pregnancy complications, neonatal care and evacuation, and to name the obstetric hospital before you land.
action: Fifteen minutes tonight with the long-haul booking open. One: her seat is an aisle on every leg, and the below-the-knee graduated compression stockings from Day 32 are in the house in her calf size — order them now if not. Two: ask the travel insurer four questions, in writing: does the policy cover complications of pregnancy abroad, including miscarriage, and to what week; does it cover a premature baby's care abroad; does it include medical evacuation and to where; is anything in her history excluded as pre-existing. Write the answers with the policy number on one page; a no or a vague answer is the thing to fix before anything non-refundable is paid. Three: open the CDC travel pages for the destination — an active Zika notice means she doesn't go; malaria means a travel-clinic appointment three to four weeks out with 'pregnant' as the first word (mefloquine or chloroquine only). Four: look up the altitude of the arrival city and hotel; above 2,750 m, the Day 46 rule applies. Then write the name and address of the nearest hospital with an obstetric unit at the destination on the same page. That page goes in the pregnancy file — tomorrow's Protocol.
